criterion_notes.c1: Fails Criterion 1 (and matches Exclusion Criterion 7: water-resource studies unrelated to household or community service access). The paper examines integrated water resources management (IWRM), agro-environmental nutrient management, and watershed-based source water protection (SWP) policy arenas in agricultural areas of Ontario, rather than household or community water or sanitation service access.
criterion_notes.c2: Plain wording vs. narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading: Under the plain wording of Criterion 2, this study WOULD satisfy Criterion 2 (plain = yes) because it examines environmental governance, policy networks, institutional scales (farm, county, watershed), and provincial legislation/programs (Environmental Farm Plan, Nutrient Management Act 2002, Clean Water Act 2006). Under the active narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading, it FAILS Criterion 2 (narrow = no) because these agro-environmental and watershed planning governance arrangements address agricultural non-point pollution and source water quality management rather than a rule-type mechanism directly governing household or community water or sanitation service access (such as eligibility screening, administrative burden, tenure/documentation rules, tariffs, enforcement, or utility regulatory structure governing service access). Note that even under the plain wording of Criterion 2, the overall study decision remains exclude because Criteria 1 and 4 fail.
criterion_notes.c3: Satisfies Criterion 3: qualitative empirical case study in Ontario (2004-2006 fieldwork covering 15 years of policy evolution) triangulating document analysis of over 60 consultation submissions and policy papers, participant observation across 63 water and farm events/committee meetings, and 11 semi-structured interviews with provincial/municipal officials and farm and environmental interest groups.
criterion_notes.c4: Fails Criterion 4: reports qualitative findings on policy-network frames of reference, stakeholder collaboration, and preferred spatial scales (farm, county, watershed) for agro-environmental water quality and source water protection, with no outcome measuring household or community water or sanitation access, connection, availability, reliability, continuity, quantity, affordability, or exclusion.
criterion_notes.c5: Within its own qualitative policy-network case-study design, the study clearly identifies the unit of analysis and sample (provincial, municipal/county, conservation authority, agricultural, and environmental policy-network actors in Ontario; 60+ documents, 63 observed events, 11 interviews), the institutional/policy processes examined, and the governance/scale outcomes, though none pertain to household or community service access.

evidence_quotes.quote: In this paper, we draw on the policy network perspective on governance to shed light on the strengths and weaknesses of watershed-based processes of collaboration and integration for water quality protection in agricultural areas.
Empirically, this study is based on the analysis of agro-environmental strategies for water quality protection in the Province of Ontario over the last 15 years.

The most important events and interactions leading to the ongoing intersection of agricultural and environmental actors in the (post-Walkerton) source water protection (SWP) policy arena are presented and discussed in the following sections.

Documentary sources included over 60 consultation submissions, position papers and commentaries generated by agricultural and environmental organizations in regard to proposed legislation for water quality protection.
For the agricultural policy network of Ontario, meaningful scales for collaboration and integration of land and water resources and interests do not currently include the watershed.

raw_response.exposure: Agro-environmental and watershed governance institutions and policy arenas in Ontario (Environmental Farm Plan, Nutrient Management Act, proposed Clean Water Act, and intersectoral agricultural vs. environmental policy networks)
raw_response.outcome: Policy-network frames of reference, stakeholder collaboration dynamics, and socially constructed spatial scales (farm, county, watershed) for agricultural water quality and source water protection
raw_response.population_and_sample: Agricultural and environmental policy networks in Ontario, Canada (unit of analysis: policy networks and stakeholder organizations; >60 policy submissions/documents, participant observation at 63 events from January 2004 to March 2006, and 11 semi-structured interviews with government officials and farm/environmental group representatives)
raw_response.rationale: Excluded as E01 (Wrong topic; per Exclusion Criterion 7, water-resource studies unrelated to household or community service access). This qualitative policy-network study analyzes integrated water resources management (IWRM), agricultural nutrient management, and watershed-based source water quality protection governance in rural Ontario. Although Walkerton's 2000 municipal well contamination is discussed as the catalyst for provincial source water protection legislation, the paper does not examine household or community water or sanitation service access (c1 = no), does not examine a rule-type legal or administrative mechanism governing service access under the 2026-10-13 Criterion 2 scope (c2 = no; plain c2 = yes, though overall plain decision is still exclude due to c1 and c4), and reports no service-access outcome (c4 = no).
raw_response.study_design: Qualitative empirical case study (policy network analysis using document analysis, participant observation, and semi-structured interviews)
